MODULE 2: FULL OUTLINE

WARM-UP

Basketball School

SMALL SPACE DRIBBLE KNOCKOUT

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed)

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per player (other loads can be performed if not enough balls for each player)

#### DESCRIPTION

Give players ten seconds to find a partner. Players can use any available space in the gym. Both players have a ball, attempting to keep their dribble alive while simultaneously knocking the ball out of their opponent's hands. Each load can be played for anywhere from 30 to 60 seconds. Change partners after two different loads have been played.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Only dribble using weak hand.
- Perform a change of direction dribble every three dribbles.
- Ball must be bounced above the waist every time.
- Ball must be bounced below the knees every time.
- One player has the ball while their partner is on defense. Offense attempts to maintain the dribble for 12 seconds without having the ball stolen or deflected.

#### SCORING

1 point for each round win.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Developing ball manipulation skills
- Stealing the ball without fouling

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players change pairs after every two rounds.
- Encourage players to scan the floor and locate the defense.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Find a way to knock out your opponent's ball."
- "How could you move the ball to trick your opponent?"

WARM-UP

Basketball School

PASS KEEPAWAY

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed). Mark out 3PT-sized playing areas with cones if needed.

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per game

#### DESCRIPTION

Players must be divided into teams of 3-on-3 (the game could be played 4-on-4 or 5-on-5 too). Players can self-select teams, but coaches can change teams if the teams are not reasonably balanced. Designate the players into different areas of the gym, such as within the 3PT area or grids of an equivalent size marked out by cones. One team must perform 10 passes in a row, without a deflection, committing a turnover or violation (e.g. stepping out of bounds, traveling, etc).

#### STAFF ROLE

- Officiate fouls and violations.
- Get teams playing as quickly as possible within their designated spaces.
- If teams do not call their pass count, call 'turnover' and the other team regains possession.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Passing against pressure
- Pivoting
- Creating leads and getting open

#### SCORING

1 point is awarded each time a team completes 10 passes in a row. If teams do not count their passes, a turnover is called and the other team gains possession.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Teams have an option to take one dribble if needed.
- If one designated player on each team catches the ball, it is worth two passes instead of one.
- Players can run dribble hand-offs with their one dribble limit.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where is the space?"
- "Defensively, how can you position yourself to make it harder for the other team to successfully pass?"

GAME TIME

Basketball School

GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

1-ON-1 ROOTED

1-ON-1 ADVANCE THE BALL

3-ON-3 HALF-COURT CONTINUOUS

1-ON-1 BLIND SHOOTING

4-ON-4 DEFENSIVE SHUTDOWN

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### I-ON-1 ROOTED

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

3 balls per group, 1 group in each half-court area.

#### DESCRIPTION

Players work in groups of four. Three offensive players have the balls and can begin in different positions outside the paint. There is one defender who can only play defense in a position close to the basket, but they are not allowed to move or jump. Each player gets two repetitions on offense before changing roles and picking a new defender. The offense must find ways to score without the rooted defender stealing or deflecting the ball.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Defenders play defense holding a ball instead of using their hands.
- If the defense steals the ball, they have five seconds to gain an additional point by immediately transitioning into a live 1-on-1.
- Offensive players have a seven dribble limit.
- Offensive players must advance with a maximum of seven dribbles but retreat dribbles do not count as part of this limit.
- Add a trailing defender to turn the activity into a 1-on-2.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 1 point for every missed shot.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Officiate fouls and violations.
- Make sure players start from different angles and locations.
- Ensure a new defender is picked after all offensive players get two repetitions.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Contesting shots without fouling (walling-up)
- Improving finishing skills

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "Where was the space to finish?"
- "What other solutions could you explore to finish?"
- "What defensive concept are we learning?"

### I-ON-I ADVANCE THE BALL

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed). Use cones to mark out grids from the elbow lane extended to the sideline on all available courts.

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Players play in pairs or in groups of three if there are high numbers. One offensive player has 10 seconds to 'advance the ball' against their defender. They must start behind the baseline and reach the half-court line without stepping out of bounds or losing control of the ball. Players manage their own rotations within their groups.

#### SCORING

Ball-handler will get 1 point if they successfully get from the half-court line to baseline within 10 seconds. The defense will get 1 point if they force a turnover or the time limit passes.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Advancing the ball against pressure
- Containing the ball on defense

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Defenders play defense holding a ball instead of using their hands.
- If the defense steals the ball, they have five seconds to gain an additional point by immediately transitioning into a live 1-on-1.
- Offensive players have a seven dribble limit.
- Offensive players must advance with a maximum of seven dribbles but retreat dribbles do not count as part of this limit.
- Add a trailing defender to turn the activity into a 1-on-2.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Count down from 10 seconds.
- Remind players to verbally communicate the score.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you contain the ball-handler without allowing a blow-by?"
- "What can you do to trick the defense?"

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### 3-ON-3 HALF-COURT CONTINUOUS

20 MIN
BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of three. Make sure each basket has a minimum of three teams per basket and a maximum of six. Teams will play half-court 3-on-3 with additional teams waiting at the baseline. After a make, the team that just got scored on sprints off while a new defensive team comes on from the baseline and touches the 3PT line before matching up and defending. Simultaneously, the offense must advance the ball and touch the half-court line to initiate the next 3-on-3.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Beating initial defense and reading second and third levels of help defense
- Identifying the open player

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What is the 'lava' load teaching?"
- "Where is the space?"

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Escape the lava. After a pass or cut is completed, the offensive player without the ball has three seconds to escape the lava (space out). If they are still inside the lava after three seconds, a turnover is called.
- Pass and cut is a turnover. Players can only create an advantage through a static 1-on-1 where the ball-handler creates an advantage with a dribble move from the perimeter, or through a post-up. Teammates should maintain spacing (following the 'lava' load), ready to receive the ball.
- Teams can be given actions to run and to emphasize as they play (on-ball screen, off-ball screen, blitz the ball-handler, etc.)

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure the players keep and communicate score.
- Make sure players start from different angles and locations.

GAME TIME

Basketball School

### I-ON-I BLIND SHOOTING

IG MIN BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players find a partner and a ball. Three groups can play 1-on-1 on the same basket at the same time. The defender will start 'blind' to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender's back. Once they lift the ball from the defense's back, it becomes a live 1-on-1. The offense has a maximum of three dribbles to score but can only score by shooting outside the paint. Each repetition should have a different starting location, beginning anywhere outside the paint.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating and maintaining advantage
- Attempting to shoot as quickly and controlled as possible
- Exploring different ways to stop (e.g. jump stop, stride stop, etc).

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defense is not allowed to block the shooter, but can distract them.
- The offense and defense must change partners after they both play offense.
- The offense can only score with one dribble.
- The offense gets double points for a swish.
- The offense begins in the paint, facing away from the basket, and must escape the lava and shoot within three dribbles.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Get the players organized to read the space and successfully organize themselves by communicating whose turn it is.
- Challenge players to get their shot off quickly before the defender can recover.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How can you use the space before the defense can recover?"
- "How can the defense rear view contest without fouling?"
